name: Documentation Writing Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for documentation writing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for documentation writing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep documentation writing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
2. Prefer explicit, readable documentation writing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. State assumptions about documentation writing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to documentation writing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. When multiple documentation writing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Document any non-obvious documentation writing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. When documentation writing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen documentation writing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
9. Validate documentation writing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
10. Measure before optimizing any documentation writing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
11. When documentation writing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated documentation writing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop documentation writing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting documentation writing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these documentation writing guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
